Chapter 8: Inspiring Willingness—Appealing to Higher Motives and Shared Values.
As our relationships grow deeper, the way we inspire action naturally becomes more thoughtful and nuanced. One of the most powerful ways you can motivate someone is by appealing to their higher motives—their sense of purpose, their integrity, or their desire to make a real difference.
Think about it: We’re not just motivated by what’s in it for us. Deep down, we’re also moved by values and ideals. When you frame a suggestion or a request around these deeper motivations, it just hits differently. It resonates more, and people feel a stronger sense of commitment.
Imagine a leader encouraging their team to hit a tough deadline. Instead of focusing only on profit, they might remind everyone that finishing on time means delivering a promise to customers—or protecting the reputation for excellence the team has worked so hard to build.
Or picture a parent guiding their child. Rather than just enforcing rules, they might appeal to the child’s sense of responsibility or kindness. It’s a subtle shift, but it makes all the difference.
The real key? It’s connecting the action you’re hoping for to something the other person already cares about. That takes empathy and a little insight—you’ve got to know what matters most to them, and then speak to those values honestly.
Here are a few ways you can inspire willingness through shared values:
Start by framing your requests in terms of purpose, integrity, or contribution. Recognize and affirm the other person’s positive intentions. Connect what you’re asking to a larger mission or shared goal. And use words that highlight meaning and impact—not just the end result.
When people feel like their actions matter on a deeper level, they’re way more likely to go above and beyond. What starts as simple compliance can turn into genuine enthusiasm—and even pride.
